title: Soft-swap speculative decode: model-health scoring + latency-budget-aware fallback
creator: Diego Park
description:
Problem: Speculative decoding (prefill + tentative decode on fast/low-cost model variants) is a major lever for latency/cost tradeoffs, but current runtime lacks a graceful soft-swap and health-driven routing layer that (1) avoids committing low-quality outputs, (2) respects per-request latency budgets, and (3) falls back without client-visible glitches.

Goal: Implement a "soft-swap" speculative-decode runtime component that uses a continuous model-health score and kernel-compatibility fingerprint to decide: whether to run a fast speculative decoder, when to commit its output, and how to fall back to a slower but higher-quality model without duplication of tokens or user-visible regressions. The component must: 1) integrate with kernel selection heuristics and attention-optimization hints, 2) emit telemetry for acceptance/rollback decisions, and 3) provide operator controls for acceptance thresholds and latency budgets.

Key design ideas (summary):
- Model-Health Score: composite signal combining recent acceptance rate, per-token quality delta (measured on sampled prompt corpus), model drift indicator (perplexity/embedding-shift), and kernel-execution success rate. Score is normalized 0..100.
- Latency-Budget Policy: per-request budget (ms) passed through request metadata or derived from route. The soft-swap uses a two-tier check: speculative candidate must be >health_thresh and expected remaining-latency <= budget_margin.
- Kernel Fingerprint Compatibility: speculative candidate and canonical fallback must share compatible kernel paths (quantization, attention kernel type). If kernels are incompatible, we prefer prefill-only speculative probe rather than full speculative commit to avoid KV reformatting costs.
- Soft-swap Commit Protocol: tentative tokens are emitted as streamed partials with tentative flag. When acceptance condition met, an atomic commit event promotes tentative tokens to final; otherwise run fallback with a fast rewind protocol that consumes the same KV state without double decoding.
- Fallback Modes: instant-fallback (cancel speculative run, start fallback), graceful-merge (allow fallback to resume from last committed token and stitch outputs), and replicate-and-decide (run both until verdict). Default is instant-fallback with telemetry-driven canaries.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: long-running rollout automation and UI; those will be follow-ups in console and rollout playbook tickets.

Success metrics: end-to-end 95th percentile latency improvement for high-frequency prompts >= 15% vs baseline while rollback rate < 2% for P99-critical routes and no user-visible output inconsistencies in integration tests.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a soft-swap speculative controller with config flags for health_threshold and latency_margin
Model-health score computation implemented and logged per-model (acceptance_rate, drift, kernel_success)
Kernel fingerprint compatibility check implemented and integrated with scheduler to avoid incompatible speculative commits
Soft-swap commit protocol implemented with streamed tentative tokens and atomic commit/rollback events
Fallback policies implemented: instant-fallback and graceful-merge with documented behavior
Telemetry dashboards capturing: speculative_attempts, commits, rollbacks, latency delta, cost delta
Automated integration tests demonstrating no duplicate tokens for rollback scenarios and deterministic commit transitions
Performance target: >=15% lower p95 latency on target route with rollback rate <2% in staging load tests
tasks: Prototype model-health scorer (simulated data) and unit tests
Add kernel fingerprint metadata to model manifests and runtime kernel selector
Implement speculative controller and soft-swap commit events in runtime core
Instrument telemetry and create dashboard (Grafana/BigQuery) for acceptance metrics
End-to-end integration tests including rollback, instant-fallback, and graceful-merge
PR review and perf runbook for canary rollout
Update runtime docs and add operator knobs in console (follow-up ticket for UI wiring)

2026-03-02 - Eng Architecture review by Asha Nair: Agreed on tentative tokens stream + atomic commit. Suggested keeping replication mode for stress tests only due to cost. Requested clear telemetry for 'tentative -> committed' transitions.

2026-03-07 - Performance run on staging: p95 for route A improved 18%, rollback rate 2.4%. Action: tune health_threshold to hit <2% rollback. Observed rare kernel mismatch causing fallback latency spike; created task to bounce kernel selector's cache.

2026-03-09 - QA: Integration test failure in graceful-merge path where token offsets misaligned on stitching. Root cause isolated to KV pointer not updated on tentative commit. Patch in PR 4189 to fix pointer update logic.
